# posthog_feature_flags (Data Source)

List the feature flags in a project. Use this to resolve the numeric `id` of each flag that already exists, so a `for_each` `import {}` block can adopt them into `posthog_feature_flag` resources. Deleted flags are left out; archived flags are included, because an archived flag still holds its key and creating a new flag with that key fails.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# List the flags in a project.
data "posthog_feature_flags" "all" {
  project_id = "12345"
}

output "flag_keys" {
  value = [for flag in data.posthog_feature_flags.all.flags : flag.key]
}

# Adopt flags that already exist, and create the rest, without writing any IDs.
#
# Each environment has its own project, and every project declares the same
# flags. Where a flag already exists (for example, created in the PostHog UI),
# the import block adopts it; where it does not, Terraform creates it. Once a
# flag is in state its import is a no-op, so the block can stay in place.
#
# The project is looked up by name rather than by ID, because a new
# environment's project ID is not known until apply. Until that project exists
# the data source finds no flags, so nothing is imported and every flag is
# created.
variable "environment" {
  type = string
}

locals {
  feature_flags = {
    "new-onboarding" = "New onboarding flow"
    "beta-dashboard" = "Beta dashboard"
  }
}

resource "posthog_project" "this" {
  name = var.environment
}

data "posthog_feature_flags" "existing" {
  project_name = var.environment
}

resource "posthog_feature_flag" "this" {
  for_each   = local.feature_flags
  project_id = posthog_project.this.id
  key        = each.key
  name       = each.value
}

# for_each in an import block needs Terraform 1.7 or later.
import {
  for_each = {
    for flag in data.posthog_feature_flags.existing.flags : flag.key => flag.id
    if contains(keys(local.feature_flags), flag.key)
  }
  to = posthog_feature_flag.this[each.key]
  id = "${data.posthog_feature_flags.existing.project_id}/${each.value}"
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

- `organization_id` (String) Organization to look `project_name` up in. Defaults to the provider-level organization_id. Only used with `project_name`.
- `project_id` (String) Project ID (environment) to list flags in. Defaults to the provider-level project_id. Conflicts with `project_name`. When the project is looked up by `project_name` and none matches, this is null.
- `project_name` (String) Name of the project to list flags in, matched case-insensitively within `organization_id`. Use this when the project ID is not known until apply, for example a project created in the same configuration. When no project has this name, `flags` is empty rather than an error. More than one project with the name is an error.

### Read-Only

- `flags` (Attributes List) The project's flags, sorted by key. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--flags))

<a id="nestedatt--flags"></a>
### Nested Schema for `flags`

Read-Only:

- `active` (Boolean) Whether the flag is enabled.
- `archived` (Boolean) Whether the flag is archived.
- `id` (Number) Numeric ID of the flag. Use `<project_id>/<id>` as the `id` in an `import {}` block.
- `key` (String) Flag key.
- `name` (String) Flag name (its description in the PostHog UI).
